column1: # config/r3-11-reel.tsv -- what R3-11's artefact shows, as DATA.
# `tools/replay-capture.py reel config/r3-11-reel.tsv` replays these captures
# into a terminal at true wire speed, in order, with a title before each.  Point
# a screen recorder at the terminal and the artefact is finished -- and, unlike
# a recording, it is REPRODUCIBLE: every byte comes from a committed capture and
# anyone who clones this repository can re-run the same command.
# 🔴 EVERY SEGMENT IS A COMMITTED CAPTURE FROM SEATING 7 (2026-08-31), and the
# reel may not contain anything else.  A reel that mixed a re-enactment in with
# real captures would be a recording again, and the whole reason this file
# exists is that it cannot.
# The order is R3's own DoD, D1 through D5, because that is the claim the
# artefact is evidence for -- not because it is the prettiest order.
# prefix<TAB>title<TAB>pause-seconds
# ⚠️ The running time is the sum of the captures' own durations plus the pauses;
# `replay-capture verify <prefix>` prints each one.
# 0.048 + 3.099 = **11.56 s of capture** plus 12.5 s of pauses = **~24 s**.
# 🔴 PROGRESS.md calls this *the 60-second artefact* and at these pauses it
# is not sixty seconds.  The number to change is the pause column, not the
# captures -- padding a reel with dead terminal is worse than a short one,
# and the capture durations are the device's, not a choice.
# 🔄 2026-09-01: THE PAUSES ARE NOT BEING PADDED, and the reason is not
# reluctance.  Six segments to 60 s is 8 s of dead terminal each, and the
# sentence above already says why that is the wrong repair.  The other
# repair is MORE CAPTURE, and seating 8 is about to produce it: probe3's
# own boot, its UART report and the 718-word read-back.  Setting this
# column now would be setting it against a reel that is about to grow, so
# it is set at R3-11 with that material in hand.  PROGRESS.md's R3-11 row
# carries the decision; this comment is the pointer, not a second owner.
